observations:
Torah #133 contains zero bechina-connected nodes and therefore zero packages can be proposed — neither existing-type nor new.

The criterion for a new package proposal is: three or more concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא used as identity) forming an independent conceptual domain. Torah #133 has zero concepts with bechina language, making the threshold unreachable by definition.

Five candidate concept-clusters were examined to determine whether any could qualify as a new package:

1. SUN / TZADDIK / LIGHT CLUSTER (שֶׁמֶשׁ, צַדִּיק, אוֹר הַגָּדוֹל): The most obvious candidate for a new package — the teaching's entire mashal-nimshal structure equates the Tzaddik to the sun and his light to the sun's light. However, this equation is made via the simile language כְּאוֹר נֹגַהּ מַמָּשׁ and כֵּן הַצַּדִּיקִים (literally-like / so-too), not via bechina-declaration language. The framework requires explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, הַיְנוּ) to assign parallel-nature relationships to packages. An analogy (mashal) is not a bechina — it illustrates by comparison rather than declaring shared essential nature. In other Torahs where the Rebbe does declare שֶׁמֶשׁ as a bechina of חָכְמָה or of the Tzaddik (e.g., Torahs #1, #6), explicit bechina language is present. Torah #133 has none.

2. EARTH / WORLD OBSTRUCTION CLUSTER (הָאָרֶץ, עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מְנִיעָה): The earth and the world are treated as the same obstruction via the mashal's narrative gloss (הָאָרֶץ הַמַּפְסֶקֶת, הַיְנוּ הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה). The word הַיְנוּ here is a mashal-clarification ('that is to say, the world is what the earth represents'), not a bechina-declaration ('the earth IS A BECHINA OF the world' in the formal ontological sense). Mashal identification is distinct from bechina declaration. No package can be formed.

3. SMALL BLOCKING OBJECT CLUSTER (מַטְבֵּעַ קְטַנָּה, יָד קְטַנָּה, עוֹלָם הַזֶּה): One might argue that the small coin, the small hand, and this world form a conceptual cluster of 'small-but-proximate obstruction'. While there is genuine thematic coherence among these three mashal variants, the Rebbe does not use any bechina language to equate them to each other or to any third concept. They are three iterations of the same mashal device for illustrative/rhetorical effect, not three bechina-equivalences that map to a shared essential nature. This does not qualify as a new package.

4. VISION / EYES CLUSTER (עֵינַיִם, הַסְתַּכְּלוּת, הַגְבָּהַת עֵינַיִם): The teaching repeatedly refers to the eyes and vision as the locus of the problem and the solution. Eyes appear in multiple roles: the world stands 'before the eyes', one must 'lift the eyes', the coin blocks 'vision'. These are all parts of the eitza chain (positioning → obstruction → limited vision; removal → clear vision) and do not constitute parallel-nature (bechina) declarations about each other.

5. GOOD/EVIL MIRROR EXAMINATION: The framework requires actively searching for an evil counterpart to every good package (section 4). In Torah #133, the 'obstruction' (world/earth/coin) functions as the negative force preventing people from accessing the light. However, even this is not developed as an evil entity with its own bechina structure — it is presented as a neutral positional fact (the world is simply very close to our eyes, like the coin) rather than as an active evil force with conceptual equivalences. There is no כּוֹחוֹת הָרָע cluster, no kelipah terminology, no evil mirror package because the teaching does not develop the negative side in conceptual terms. The world's smallness and proximity is described with the coin metaphor — it is a natural phenomenon, not a malevolent force given bechina-identity.

CONCLUSION: The complete absence of bechina-type relationships in Torah #133 is a genuine structural feature of this teaching, not a dataset gap. Torah #133 is one of Rebbe Nachman's most accessible and practically-oriented teachings, organized as an extended analogy with a clear eitza conclusion rather than as a kabbalistic concept-mapping exercise. The mashal structure (sun/earth, coin/mountain, hand/eyes) is entirely analogical, not ontological. NO_NEW_PACKAGES.
